headline: Senators’ William Eklund out 10-to-12 weeks with torn tendon in ankle
take:
Per Daily Faceoff, Ottawa's William Eklund is out 10 to 12 weeks with a torn tendon in his ankle. The report adds that Artem Zub is expected to make his 2026-27 debut Thursday against the Islanders.

Eklund's four games so far this season were quietly strong. He generated 2.66 expected goals against just 1 actual goal, a gap of -1.66, so his scoring is likely to bounce back and losing him costs more than two points suggests. The Senators controlled 68.75 percent of 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share of expected goals was 27.72 percentage points better with him in the lineup. That is a small sample, but it is a big swing for a team sitting at 6-2-0 with a 47 percent 5-on-5 expected goals share overall, so there is little cushion. Zub's return helps, though his one game so far this season saw Ottawa at 43.36 percent at 5-on-5 and 3.01 points worse overall. He played 18.48 minutes, so he slots straight into a top-four role. Ottawa's power play (0.88 expected goals per game) is where Eklund's absence may show first.
